newsitem.title: USA: TCF Financial to buy Standard Financial.
newsitem.headline: TCF Financial to buy Standard Financial.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp. has a definitive agreement to acquire Standard Financial Inc., a Chicago-based banking company, in a deal worth about $424 million in cash and stock, the companies said Monday.
The combined company would have $10 billion in assets and 276 financial services offices and more than 900 automatic teller machines in five Midwest states.

TCF, a savings bank holding company based in Minneapolis, will offer about $25 for each Standard share in a purchase transaction. Standard stockholders may choose to receive cash or TCF shares or a combination of the two. Between 40 percent and 60 percent of the purchase would be paid in TCF stock, and the rest in cash.
The exchange ratio for shares would depend on the average price of TCF stock during the 30 trading days before the deal closes.
The stock portion of the deal is tax-free for Standard stockholders.
Standard's stock rose $2.375 to $23.50 early on Nasdaq. TCF fell 75 cents to $43.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
TCF said it expects the merger to boost earnings in 1998.
"We believe this merger will produce long-term revenue enhancements and meaningful cost savings," TCF Chairman William Cooper said in a statement.

"Joining TCF will accelerate our transformation to a leading consumer bank, for the benefit of our shareholders, customers, and the communities we serve," added Standard Chairman and President David Mackiewich.
TCF said it would record "intangibles" of about $200 million in connection with the deal.

The merger is expected to close in the third quarter, subject to approval by Standard's stockholders and regulators. The definitive agreement was signed after completion of due diligence and approval of both companies' boards.
Standard has agreed to pay TCF $15 million if the deal does not close under certain circumstances.
Standard also said it postponed its annual meeting and plans to call a special meeting to seek stockholder approval of the merger.
Standard, a thrift institution with $2.4 billion in assets, has 14 full-service offices on the southwest side of Chicago and in nearby suburbs.

TCF, which has $7.1 billion in assets, operates more than 260 financial services offices in Minnesota, Illinois, and Wisconsin as TCF Bank, and in Michigan and Ohio as Great Lakes Bancorp. It also has affiliates in consumer finance, mortgage banking, title insurance, annuity and mutual fund sales.
